key_insight: A single, learnable view-adaptive curve module jointly corrects color (chromatic) and lightness (photometric) differences across views, restoring photometric consistency and enabling robust novel view synthesis from real-world captures.
problem_solved: Multi-view images captured in the wild suffer from illumination, sensor and ISP differences that break photometric consistency assumptions of modern NVS/NeRF methods, producing color and brightness artifacts in synthesized views.
method: Learn a parametric curve-based correction that models both chromatic (color) and lightness adjustments, applied in image space.
Predict view-adaptive curve parameters conditioned on per-view features (and geometry/latent scene cues) so each capture gets a tailored correction.
Integrate the differentiable curve module into the NVS training loop so corrected inputs and synthesis are jointly optimized for improved rendering quality.
impact: Makes NeRF-style and other novel-view synthesis systems much more robust to real-world capture variability, reducing color/brightness artifacts and improving fidelity without complex pre-processing — accelerating deployment on unconstrained multi-view datasets.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view inputs → view-adaptive curve module → corrected images → NeRF synthesis (novel view output).
Before/after image triplets showing color/lightness mismatches and corrected synthesized view.
Example learned per-view curves (RGB + lightness axes) illustrating how different captures are adjusted.
Quantitative bar chart or table comparing metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) and error maps before vs after correction.
paper_title: Unifying Color and Lightness Correction with View-Adaptive Curve Adjustment for Robust 3D Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Ziteng Cui, Shuhong Liu, Xiaoyu Dong, Xuangeng Chu, Lin Gu
